system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present with suitable encodings (GSM-7 for en, UCS-2 for ar). There are two fixable problems. First, neither language fits the UAE one-page handset guidance: en is 3 pages and ar is 6. Second, neither text contains any protective action, so the first page carries only the hazard.

objections.issue: Both language versions exceed the UAE one-page guidance: English (221 chars, GSM-7) is 3 pages and Arabic (229 chars, UCS-2) is 6 pages. Handsets may show only part of the alert, and pages can arrive or display out of order.
objections.fix: Condense each language to fit one CBS page (about 93 GSM-7 characters for en and about 41 UCS-2 characters for ar). Keep the hazard, the area, the validity time and the action. Drop secondary detail such as the full source attribution and the exact visibility figure, or move it to a link or follow-up. If ar cannot fit hazard and action in one UCS-2 page, at minimum put both in the first page.

evidence.quote: message should be limited to 1 page
the BSC sends to the BTS in one single message the 88 octet fixed length CBS page

objections.issue: Neither the English nor the Arabic text tells the public what to do (no protective action). The first page carries only the hazard description: in en it stops mid-sentence at 'under 2,'; in ar it carries only the opening wind description.
objections.fix: Add a short protective action as specified by the issuing authority, for example to reduce outdoor activity, drive with caution and lower speed, and take care if they have respiratory conditions. Place it in the first page of both en and ar, immediately after the hazard.
